statement: Ella folds a paper square in half and cuts 3 small shapes through both layers: 2 away from the fold, 1 right on the fold. How many holes are there when she opens it?

choices.misconception: I counted only the holes on one side of the fold and left out the hole on the fold.
I forgot that the scissors cut through both layers, so I counted one hole for each shape.
I counted two holes for each shape away from the fold and forgot the shape on the fold.
I thought every shape makes two holes, even the one cut right on the fold.

hints: What happens to a shape cut right on the fold?
The scissors go through both layers, so a shape away from the fold makes a hole on each half. A shape cut on the fold opens out into one hole across the fold. Count each kind.
The 2 shapes away from the fold make 2 holes each, which is 4 holes. The shape on the fold opens into just one hole.

solutions.reliable: Each shape away from the fold is cut through both layers, so it makes one hole on each half of the opened square: 2 shapes make 4 holes. The shape on the fold opens out into a single hole that crosses the fold, so it adds just 1. That makes 4 + 1 = 5 holes. The idea to keep: the fold works like a mirror, and a shape sitting on the mirror line is its own match.

whyOnTest: Folding and cutting shows a line of symmetry at work: every hole has a partner across the fold, except one sitting on the fold.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
